what_it_does: This paper describes a 3D NAND flash memory chip—the type that stores data in many layers stacked vertically to pack more storage into the same footprint. The challenge: as you stack hundreds of layers, several problems appear. Extra strings of transistors take up space and draw power; control signals for writing data (wordlines) degrade cells in unintended layers; and the wiring connecting all these layers creates timing delays that slow down the chip. This design tackles all three by: removing wasted dummy structures, restructuring how control signals reach individual layers, and carefully optimizing the pin layout to maintain signal quality at 5.6 gigabits per second per pin. The result is a 1 terabit chip at 28 gigabits per square millimeter, storing 3 bits per storage cell.
